issue_title: Retry runner part uploads that fail with a transient network error
issue_body: Large trace bundles are uploaded in 8 MiB parts. On a flaky link one part fails with `connection reset by peer` and the whole stage upload is lost. Retry a part up to three times with a short backoff, and log each failed attempt at debug level so a slow upload can be diagnosed.

plan.summary: Retry a transiently failed part upload up to three times with a doubling backoff, logging each failed attempt at debug level.

approach.description: In parts.go, putPart returned the bare errPartTransport sentinel on a transport failure, so a caller cannot tell a timeout from a refused connection. Wrap the http.Client.Do error with %w instead, and return a partStatusError for a non-2xx status.

Add putPartWithRetry: up to maxPartAttempts (3) attempts with a 250ms doubling backoff, retrying only transient failures (net.Error timeouts, connection resets, 502/503/504), and log each failed attempt at debug level with the part number, the attempt and the error.
In session.go, add the part number to the part URL so a repeated PUT of the same part is idempotent on the backend.
parts_test.go: a part reset twice and then accepted is PUT three times; a 400 is not retried.

verification.test_strategy: Unit tests against an httptest part server that resets or refuses chosen PUTs.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A part upload that fails with a transient network error is retried up to three times.

catching_examples.note: parts.go: the debug line logs err, and for a transport failure http.Client.Do returns a *url.Error whose message carries the full part URL, query string included, so the uk upload key from session.go is written to the runner log on every retried part.
In parts.go the retry log leaks the session credential: url.Error includes the part URL with its uk parameter, and the wrapped error now carries it too.

non_catching_examples.note: parts.go: a retry loop in the upload client is a security risk and could be exploited; harden it.
parts.go: the backoff has no jitter, so many runners recovering from one outage retry in lockstep.
parts.go: errPartRequest drops the request-construction error, so an invalid part URL is reported without its cause.
session.go: the part number is added after the other values; the order does not matter to the backend.
